about.title: About
about.dek: Seoul, then Evanston. Lasers, thin films, and the images of a melt pool.
paragraphs: I am a Ph.D. student in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at Northwestern University, in the Fast-AM Laboratory with Professor Tao Sun. I am also a visiting graduate student in the XSD-IMG group at the Advanced Photon Source (APS), Argonne National Laboratory.

I was born and raised in Seoul. I earned a B.S. in mechanical engineering at Hanyang University, Summa Cum Laude, and an M.S. in mechanical convergence engineering there, in the Smart Manufacturing Laboratory with Professor Seung Hwan Lee. An interest in automobiles — from Hot Wheels to Formula One — brought me into mechanical engineering. Lasers held me there: a manufacturing tool in the automotive, aerospace, shipbuilding, and semiconductor industries.

As an undergraduate I studied multi-axis laser metal deposition, and how nozzle tilt and substrate inclination change the quality of Inconel 625. In the master’s I contributed to South Korea’s first laser spallation system, a pulsed-laser shock-wave method for the adhesion of thin films, and I worked on physics-informed machine learning for fatigue life and for proton-exchange membrane fuel cells.

The doctorate is about laser–material interaction and defect formation in additive manufacturing, watched with operando synchrotron x-ray imaging, including multi-element stranded wire laser directed energy deposition (L-DED). Part of that work is SMAXI, open-source software for full-field x-ray images. I am a Predictive Science and Engineering Design (PS&ED) Cluster Fellow for 2026–2027.

research.title: Research
research.dek: Operando x-ray imaging of laser additive manufacturing, the software that reads those images, and earlier work on thin-film adhesion and physics-informed prediction.

cards.title: Operando imaging of multi-element stranded wire laser directed energy deposition (L-DED)
cards.body: With the Advanced Photon Source (APS), Argonne National Laboratory, in Lemont, I use high-speed synchrotron x-ray imaging to watch multi-element stranded wire laser directed energy deposition (L-DED) while it runs. The experiments sit with the Fast-AM Laboratory’s work on energy–matter interaction and how defects are generated.

cards.title: SMAXI
cards.body: SMAXI is open-source software for multidimensional full-field x-ray image analysis. It brings in current machine-learning models for object annotation and tracking. Professor Tao Sun and I are corresponding authors on the Journal of Synchrotron Radiation paper.

cards.title: Laser spallation
cards.body: Laser spallation is a pulsed-laser shock-wave test for the interfacial adhesion of thin films. Peel and stud-pull tests grip the film and mix plastic deformation into the number; the shock wave does not. During my master’s at Hanyang I contributed to South Korea’s first laser spallation system — pulsed-laser optics and a Michelson interferometer — in work that included packaging reliability with SK Hynix. The thesis measured LPCVD silicon nitride and copper (UCI: I804:11062-200000826436).

cards.title: Multi-axis laser metal deposition
cards.body: Curved surfaces and overhangs — a propeller blade, a rocket-engine casing — need the nozzle or the substrate tilted. Powder flowing on that incline is easy to get wrong. My undergraduate work on Inconel 625 mapped how process parameters, including laser power and beam diameter, change deposition quality at extreme angles, and turned that map into a guideline. The undergraduate thesis was a Gaussian-process model of the deposit geometry.

cards.title: Physics-informed prognostics
cards.body: A black-box model needs more experiments than a process lab can afford, and it does not carry the mechanics. With co-first authors I worked on a physics-informed Gaussian process for the fatigue life of welded joints, and a physics-informed neural network for the remaining life of proton-exchange membrane fuel cells.

lab.name: Fast-AM Laboratory
lab.place: Department of Mechanical Engineering, Northwestern University · 2145 Sheridan Rd, Evanston, IL 60208
lab.summary: The Fast-AM Laboratory investigates fundamental issues in advanced manufacturing with in situ and ex situ characterization. The group’s present focus is energy–matter interaction, mass and heat flow, defect generation, and how structure develops in additive manufacturing, toward manufacturing technology for a more sustainable industrial future.
approaches: Laser powder bed fusion and wire-laser directed energy deposition
Binder jetting and direct ink writing
High-speed x-ray imaging, high-energy diffraction, and 4D x-ray imaging
Multi-physics simulation, molecular dynamics, and CALPHAD
Machine learning for in-process defect detection and simulation optimization

pastLab.name: Smart Manufacturing Laboratory
pastLab.place: Department of Mechanical Engineering, Hanyang University, Seoul
pastLab.summary: The Smart Manufacturing Laboratory works on making conventional manufacturing smarter. The group combines process technology with lasers, artificial intelligence, metallurgy, and CFD — both to develop processes that had not been tried and to apply AI so production costs fall.
